# `prefer-early-return`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: none · Default: off · Fixes: quick fix · Options: none

Reports an `if` whose `else` block contains only a return while the main path
continues.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Inverting the condition into an early-return guard lets the main path continue
at the surrounding indentation level.

## When it fires

The else block must contain exactly one return statement, and the `if` must
not be the last link of an `else if` chain, which has no single condition to
invert. An `if` whose block also ends by leaving (`return`, `break`,
`continue`, `unreachable`, a panic or exit, or an `if`/`else` chain every
branch of which leaves) is not reported: both branches are exits and there is
no main path to unindent.

The quick fix inverts the condition (an `==` becomes `!=`, a `!operand` loses
its `!`, anything else is negated as a group), moves the return into the `if`,
and moves the main path out of its block one level. It is offered only when
that cannot change meaning or layout: the `if` is a statement on a line of its
own with a one-line condition, no comment sits between the rearranged pieces,
and the main path holds no `defer` or `errdefer` and declares no name the rest
of the enclosing block uses. It is not applied by `check --fix`, because the
rewrite is a judgment about readability.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn first(items: []const u32) !u32 {
    var value: u32 = 0;
    if (items.len != 0) {
        value = items[0];
    } else {
        return error.Empty;
    }
    return value + 1;
}
```
